title: Joe Washington in the NFL: 1979 Catch Leader and Super Bowl Champ
question: What did Joe Washington accomplish in the NFL after Oklahoma?
answer: Joe Washington (OU 1972-75), the No. 4 overall pick in 1976, led the NFL with 82 receptions for the Colts in 1979, made the Pro Bowl that season and won Super Bowl XVII with Washington after the 1982 season.
summary: OU legend Joe Washington led the NFL with 82 catches in 1979, made the Pro Bowl and won Super Bowl XVII. A look at the former Sooner's nine-season NFL career.
body: Joe Washington (OU 1972-75) left Norman as one of the most dazzling runners the program has ever produced. The Crockett, Texas, native piled up 3,995 rushing yards and 5,781 all-purpose yards, was a unanimous All-American in 1974 and a first-team pick in 1975, and helped the Sooners to national titles in both seasons. Barry Switzer called him "my greatest player."

The San Diego Chargers drafted him fourth overall in 1976, but his NFL breakout came after a 1978 trade to the Colts. He rushed for 956 yards that first season in Baltimore, and in 1979 he became one of the league's most versatile weapons, leading the NFL with 82 receptions for 750 yards while adding 884 rushing yards. That season earned him his Pro Bowl selection.

Washington moved to Washington in 1981 and had another big year, with 916 rushing yards and 70 catches. He was part of the club that won Super Bowl XVII after the 1982 season, and he spent four seasons there before closing his career with the Atlanta Falcons in 1985.

Across nine NFL seasons he totaled 4,839 rushing yards and 395 receptions for 3,413 yards, according to NFL.com. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 2005, a fitting honor for a player whose shifty style still gets Sooner fans talking.
